build: web v0.717 (android v0.682 = 120 / offset 24 - do not port)
lane_impact: L2 skills-meters blocker (3) and L8 ui-hud. FOCUS_MAX = 192 [CONTRACT, web v0.717]. FOCUS_BAR_ZERO = 48, FOCUS_BAR_SPAN = 144 - the HUD widget must subtract 48 from both operands or the bar will read non-empty exactly when the game shows it empty and prints the stance-lock caption.
text: The Focus/reload meter has a hard maximum and the HUD does NOT draw it from zero. §1t99s0§.as:249 'this.§1t4415s0§ = 8 * 24;' is the ONLY write to maxFocus anywhere in the 5,162-line player class (grep '§1t4415s0§ *=' returns exactly one line), so FOCUS_MAX = 192 in web v0.717. Android MCSPlayer.as:239 'this.maxreload = 5 * 24;' = 120 - a 60% difference, so anyone porting the meter from the android blobs gets the wrong scale and every derived ratio wrong with it. Second half, and it is the part a recreation will get wrong silently: the HUD bar is NOT focus/maxFocus. §1t113s0§.as:328 'var _loc3_:Number = (param1 - 48) / (param2 - 48);' clamped at :329-332 to a floor of 0 - the visible bar's zero point is 48, its span is 144, and displayed fill f maps to focus = 48 + 144f. The android twin uses a different offset (MCSPlayer.as:1163 'this.tempreload = this.reload - 24;'). This is why the bar reads EMPTY at exactly the focus level where a stance switch becomes affordable, and it closes the 'max' third of RR:195 blocker (3) 'Focus numerics (max/fill/switch-cost)' with a measured number instead of a Ruffle session.

ledger_text: | **In combat** | **Hard lock** — "CANNOT CHANGE STANCE" appears the instant a fight starts | [CONTRACT] |
text: The single TextField sitting on the Focus bar is a THREE-STATE readout, and the ledger has it as a one-state lock. §1t113s0§.as:336-343: at ratio == 0 it shows §1t5204s0§, set at :111 to "<font color='#BBBBBB'>" + getString(960) + '</font>' - light grey, and the frame at duel_dense 429.0 shows that grey text reading 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE'. At :344-347, while 0 < ratio < 1, the field is HIDDEN. At :348-358, at ratio >= 1, it switches to §1t5203s0§, set at :110 to "<font color='#000000'>" + getString(175) + '</font>' - black - and strings.json['175'] resolves getString(175) to 'Critical Hit', with :352 firing §1t1516s0§('Snd_criticalDamage') exactly once on the transition into that state. So the game's own HUD names the full meter a CRIT state, which is independent corroboration that the full-meter branch at §1t99s0§.as:3272 is the crit and not something else. NOTE THE STRING-TABLE HOLE, stated plainly: getString(960) has NO entry in the v0.682 table (strings.json numeric ids run 0-9010, 1893 present, nothing between 940 and 980), so the empty-state caption TEXT is recoverable ONLY from a frame. The measurement docs and the code both fail here and the film does not.

build: web v0.717 vs android v0.682 — a real roster divergence
lane_impact: L2 skills-meters: the 75-skill roster must be labelled v0.682. At least three v0.717 skills (1074/1075/1076) sit outside it with no row, no chi cost and no cooldown recoverable from any table — a hole the '75 skills' count currently hides.
text: The three per-stance full-Focus evade passives are keyed on skill ids 1074, 1075 and 1076 (§1t120s0§.as:108/:110/:112, 'public static var ...:int = 1074/1075/1076'), and THOSE IDS ARE NOT IN skilldata.xml. I checked the table directly: reference/extracted/skilldata.xml carries ids 1000-1073 plus 1500 and 1501; grep '<id>107[0-9]</id>' returns 1070,1071,1072,1073 and stops. resolved_names.json['skilldata.xml']['resolved'] likewise ends at 1073. Two consequences the corpus has nowhere. (1) The 75-skill table is the ANDROID v0.682 skill set (C2: those four XMLs are android-sourced), and web v0.717 references at least three skills it does not contain - so '75 skills' is a v0.682 count, not a v0.717 count, and the skill roster has an unmeasured build delta. (2) The names and descriptions of 1074-1076 are UNRESOLVABLE from any extracted table; the only artifact that names them is film - the skill card at reference/frames/zFtCaTO0_1M/seg-03/frames/frame_0013.jpg reads '(PASSIVE SKILL) / ALLOWS YOU TO EVADE ATTACKS WHILE SLASHING IN THIS STANCE WHEN YOUR FOCUS BAR IS FULL.' This is a clean instance of the standing invariant: the payload table and the frame disagree about what skills exist, and THE FRAME WINS.

build: both — the point IS the divergence
lane_impact: Lane-wide. Every combat row sourced from an android blob needs a WEB re-read before it can be graded CONTRACT, and the C2 caveat should be widened from 'the four data XMLs' to 'all android-sourced combat tuning'. Concretely: Heavy is x1.4 in web and x1.5 in android on BOTH damage and (for Light) reach, and the mastery coefficient differs by a factor of 10 in shape.
ledger_text: 3. **The stance tables (dmg 0.9/1.2/1.4, reach 300/200/100) are MASTERY-9 CEILING values, not base.**
quote: web §1t99s0§.as:3270 '_loc2_ = _loc1_ * 1.4;' ‖ android MCSPlayer.as:3213 'maxDamage = baseDamage * 1.5;' ‖ web :3094 'this.§1t4417s0§ = this.§1t4420s0§ * 1.4;' ‖ android :3030 'this.slashLength = this.baseSlashLength * 1.5;'
text: The build-parity trap this packet flags for CRIT_MULT is not a one-off; the android damage and reach tuning diverges from web across the board, so the android blobs are unsafe as a source for ANY combat number. Reading the two twins side by side: DAMAGE - web §1t99s0§.as:3262 Light '_loc1_ * (0.5 + 0.4 * mastery * 0.1)' vs android MCSPlayer.as:3205 'baseDamage * (0.5 + 0.5 * lightMastery * 0.01)'; web :3265 Balanced '(1 + 0.2 * mastery * 0.1)' vs android :3208 '(1 + 0.5 * balancedMastery * 0.01)'; web :3270 Heavy '_loc1_ * 1.4' vs android :3213 'baseDamage * 1.5'. REACH - web :3094 Light 'this.§1t4420s0§ * 1.4' vs android :3030 'this.baseSlashLength * 1.5'; web :3105 Balanced '(1 + 0.2 * mastery * 0.1)' vs android :3041 '(1 + 0.5 * balancedMastery * 0.01)'. METER - web max 192 vs android 120; web stance-switch cost a flat 48 vs android proportional (maxreload/3 or -maxreload/6). Every one of these is a number a ledger row could be built on. The mastery terms are not even the same shape: web multiplies mastery by 0.1, android by 0.01, so the two builds' mastery curves are on different scales and a value 'confirmed' in one is meaningless in the other.

lane_impact: L8 rebirth-elements: the dan ladder can be graded CONTRACT on WEB evidence with no android caveat, and the wiki garble is not merely noted but resolved — 'kyudan' is STAT_DAN 8 of a 0-9 range, so the display is off-by-one from the state and MAX_DAN_RANK=10 is a state count, not a rank.
ledger_text: 7. **`MAX_DAN_RANK=10` and `tenthGold=100` should be INFERRED, not CONTRACT.** The only wiki datum is garbled ("dan rank 5 (kyudan)" — kyudan=9th)
text: The dan titles do not depend on the v0.682 string table at all, because the WEB build hardcodes the ladder twice - once by string id and once in plain ASCII. §1t408s0§.as:532-566 switches on the same dan value and writes literals: case 0 '' · 1 '(nidan)' · 2 '(sandan)' · 3 '(yondan)' · 4 '(godan)' · 5 '(rokudan)' · 6 '(nanadan)' · 7 '(hachidan)' · 8 '(kyudan)' · 9 and default '(judan)', each of dan 3-5 appending getString(465), dan 6-7 getString(466), dan 8-9 and default getString(467). Set that beside §1t5957s0§.as:3063-3102, which for the same cases writes getString(456)..getString(464) resolving in strings.json to (弐段)(参段)(四段)(五段)(六段)(七段)(八段)(九段)(十段): nidan=弐段, sandan=参段, ... judan=十段, and the SAME shogo boundaries. Two independent web-side renderings agreeing rank-for-rank is a direct discharge of the S0-3 UI-copy caveat FOR THIS ROW, and it also re-proves from the web build alone that displayed dan = STAT_DAN + 1 (state 1 prints 'nidan', the second dan). It further kills the wiki 'dan rank 5 (kyudan)' garble that RR:164-165 rests on: kyudan is STAT_DAN 8, not 5.

quote: §1t99s0§.as:3274 'return _loc2_ * 1.3 + this.§1t1243s0§;' ‖ android MCSPlayer.as:3217-3221 'if(this.stance != LIGHT_STANCE) { return maxDamage * 1.2 + this.STAT_CRITICALDMG; } return maxDamage * 1.5 + this.STAT_CRITICALDMG;'
text: RR:190 combat-core blocker (2) is 'crit 1.3 vs 3 final — read one crit popup.' No popup is needed and none can be more authoritative than this: web §1t99s0§.as:3274 returns '_loc2_ * 1.3 + this.§1t1243s0§' — a flat x1.3 on the post-stance damage, plus the additive crit-damage stat, in every stance. RR:152's 'Keep CRIT_MULT=1.3' is therefore CONTRACT on target-build source rather than wiki-sourced, and RR:153's explanation of the '3x' folklore as 1.3x compounded with a per-stance crit-damage stat is CONTRADICTED in its specifics: the web crit branch has no per-stance term at all — the stance multiplier is applied BEFORE the branch at :3262-3270 and the crit leg adds only the flat 1.3 and §1t1243s0§ (= STAT_CRITICALDMG, android MCSPlayer.as:3219). WHERE A PER-STANCE CRIT DOES EXIST is the ANDROID build, and it is not 1.82: MCSPlayer.as:3215-3221 crits at x1.2 outside Light and x1.5 in Light. So the 'Heavy x1.82' figure in RR:153 matches neither build's code.

text: RR:195 skills-meters blocker (3) is 'Focus numerics (max/fill/switch-cost)'. All three are in web source and the whole meter contract is recoverable. MAX: §1t99s0§.as:249 'this.§1t4415s0§ = 8 * 24;' = 192. FILL: :1203-1205 '+1' per tick while below max. SWITCH COST: gate :3050 'this.§1t4414s0§ >= 48' and debit :3162 '-= 48' (in battle only). BONUS: :3320 '+= 6' clamped to max at :3321-3323. SLASH DEBIT, per stance: :3302 '-= this.slashUsage / 2' (Light), :3306 '-= this.slashUsage' (Balanced), :3310 '-= this.slashUsage * 1.5' (Heavy), floored at 0 by :3312-3314. CRIT SPEND: the full bar, :3295-3297. THE TRAP: the android twin's max is DIFFERENT — MCSPlayer.as:239 'this.maxreload = 5 * 24;' = 120 — so every ratio expressed as a fraction of the bar (48/192 = 1/4 web vs 48/120 = 2/5 android) diverges between builds. Under S0-3 a recreation that ported the meter from the android blobs would have a 60%-size Focus bar and a crit that arms 40% too often. The v0.717 target is 192.
